meta.purpose: Stress-test /learn-datalake recall via realistic persona queries

personas.margaret: Margaret Chen — Pratt & Whitney propulsion engineer. Asks about tables, requirements traceability, thermal/mechanical specs, vendor deliverables, unit consistency.
personas.jennifer: Jennifer Cheung — NIWC Pacific systems engineer. Asks about cybersecurity controls, interface specs, protocol tables, MITRE techniques, RMF compliance.

levels.table_ops: Work with extracted tables (read, compute, compare)
levels.quality: Find extraction failures through real usage

scenarios.query: Find me all the thermal limit tables in the datalake.
How many documents in the datalake contain requirements?
Find all documents that discuss access control policies.
scenarios.tests: BM25 text search, cybersecurity domain terms

scenarios.query: Show me all figures that depict stress analysis or fatigue curves.
List every document source URL in the datalake. How many came from .gov domains?
Are there any equations in the datalake? Show me the LaTeX.
scenarios.tests: equation block discovery, LaTeX content retrieval

scenarios.query: Find all sections titled 'Executive Summary' across every document.
scenarios.tests: section title search, cross-doc section matching

scenarios.query: Which documents mention 'titanium alloy' or 'Inconel'?
Do we have any NIST 800-series documents in the datalake?
scenarios.tests: document type discovery by naming convention

scenarios.query: Find all tables with more than 5 columns.
Show me all chunks from page 1 of each document. I want to see the title pages.
How many chunks are empty or have less than 10 words of content?
Find documents that contain both tables and figures on the same page.
Which vendor names appear most frequently across all documents?
Show me the table of contents from the longest document in the datalake.
Find any content about 'fatigue life' or 'crack propagation'.
Are there any documents in languages other than English?
List all unique section titles across the entire datalake.
Find all references to CVE identifiers in the datalake.
How many documents were extracted in the last 30 days?
Find all appendices across all documents.
Show me any content about vibration testing or modal analysis.
Which documents have the most figures? I want to know which ones are diagram-heavy.
Find all tables that have a column labeled 'Requirement' or 'Req ID'.
scenarios.tests: table header search, column name matching

scenarios.query: Show me the bibliography or references section from any document.
Find me the thermal limits table and tell me the maximum allowable temperature.
scenarios.tests: table value extraction, specific cell lookup

scenarios.query: Take that temperature value and convert it from Fahrenheit to Celsius.
Find the data rate table for any communication protocol. What's the maximum throughput?
Show me a table with numerical data. Calculate the mean and standard deviation of any numeric column.
Find a table that lists risk levels. How many items are rated 'High' or 'Critical'?
Find two tables about similar topics. Are the column headers the same?
Show me a compliance matrix table. Which requirements are marked as 'Not Met'?
Find a table with units in the header. Are the units consistent within each column?
Show me the largest table in the datalake by row count.
scenarios.tests: table size ranking, row count metadata

scenarios.query: Find a table that spans multiple pages. Was it extracted as one table or split?
Find a table with merged header cells. Did the extraction preserve the hierarchy?
Show me the HTML of that table. Is it valid HTML or does it have broken tags?
scenarios.tests: table HTML quality, S05 output validation

scenarios.query: Find a table and export it as CSV so I can open it in Excel.
Find tables about material properties. Can you interpolate a value between two rows?
Show me a table with status indicators (pass/fail, yes/no, compliant/non-compliant). Summarize the pass rate.
Find a table with dates. Sort the rows chronologically.
scenarios.tests: date parsing in table cells, sorting

scenarios.query: Show me two tables from different documents that could be joined on a common column.
Find a table where some cells are empty. What percentage of cells have missing data?
scenarios.tests: table completeness analysis, sparse cell detection

scenarios.query: Show me a table that has footnotes or annotations. Were they extracted?
Find a table with numeric ranges (e.g., '10-15', '200-300'). Parse the min and max from each range.
Find two documents that discuss the same topic. Compare their conclusions.
Which topics appear in the most documents? Give me a frequency distribution.
Find tables about the same subject in different documents. Do they agree on the values?
scenarios.tests: cross-doc table value comparison, conflict detection

scenarios.query: Show me all documents that reference the same standard (e.g., NIST, ISO, MIL-STD).
Find duplicate content across documents. Are any chunks nearly identical?
Which documents cite each other? Build a citation graph.
Find a parameter that appears in multiple documents with different values. Which is authoritative?
Compare the section structures of two similar documents. Are they organized the same way?
Find all documents that were published by the same organization.
Which security controls are mentioned across the most documents?
Find the earliest and latest documents in the datalake. How has the terminology changed?
Show me all acronym definitions across the datalake. Are any acronyms defined differently in different documents?
Find all test results tables across documents. Which tests were run on the same component?
Build a glossary from all documents. Show me terms that appear in more than 3 documents.
Find two documents that contradict each other on a specific claim. Show me both passages.
Which documents share the most similar vocabulary? Cluster them by topic.
Find a requirement in document A. Does document B satisfy it? Show me the evidence.
How many documents reference MITRE ATT&CK techniques? Map technique IDs to documents.
Find all revision histories or change logs across documents.
Which documents have overlapping scope? Show me the scope statements side by side.
Find all requirements that use the word 'shall'.
Show me requirements that have traceability IDs. How many don't have IDs?
Find requirements about temperature limits. What range of values do they specify?
Show me all security requirements. Categorize them by control family (AC, IA, SC, etc.).
Find requirements that reference other requirements by ID. Build a dependency tree.
How many requirements come from tables vs inline text? Which extraction method caught more?
Find requirements with quantitative values (numbers, ranges, tolerances). List them.
Show me requirements marked as 'derived' or 'allocated'. How do they trace to parent requirements?
Find requirements that are ambiguous — using words like 'may', 'should', 'adequate', 'sufficient'.
Compare requirements across two versions of the same document. What was added, changed, or deleted?
Find requirements that specify test methods. Cross-reference with test result tables.
Show me duplicate requirements across documents. Same text, different IDs.
Find conflicting requirements — two requirements that specify different values for the same parameter.
How many requirements have associated rationale? Show me ones without rationale.
Build a requirements traceability matrix from all requirements in the datalake.
Find requirements that changed between document revisions but kept the same ID.
Show me requirements from table rows. Were the table headers correctly used as context?
Find 'negative' requirements — things the system shall NOT do.
How many requirements mention specific materials? Group them by material.
Find requirements without a clear verification method. Flag them for review.
This section text looks like OCR garbage — random characters and broken words. Which documents have this problem?
scenarios.tests: OCR quality detection, garbled text identification

scenarios.query: I searched for 'authentication' and got zero results, but I know that NIST doc discusses it. Why didn't recall find it?
scenarios.tests: recall failure diagnosis, embedding quality, BM25 coverage

scenarios.query: This table has the wrong number of columns — the HTML shows 4 but the original PDF has 6. The extraction merged columns.
scenarios.tests: table column count validation, S05 extraction accuracy

scenarios.query: The section boundaries are wrong — Section 3 includes content that should be in Section 4. Show me the boundary.
scenarios.tests: section boundary accuracy, S04 split point error

scenarios.query: Why does this document have 3 chunks but the similar document has 47? They're roughly the same length.
The table caption says 'Table 5: Risk Assessment' but the table content is about network topology. The caption is from a different table.
This figure description says 'A diagram showing...' but it's actually a photograph. The VLM got it wrong.
The same paragraph appears in three different chunks. Why was it duplicated?
scenarios.tests: content duplication detection, S07 dedup failure

scenarios.query: The header row of this table was extracted as body text instead of as part of the table. Show me the chunk.
scenarios.tests: table boundary detection, header row missed by S05

scenarios.query: Footnotes from the bottom of the page got mixed into the body text of the section above. Where's the boundary?
The page numbers are embedded in the extracted text ('... analysis on page 47 of 128...'). They should have been stripped.
Two-column layout text got merged into a single paragraph, reading across columns instead of down. Show me the broken text.
scenarios.tests: column layout detection, reading order error

scenarios.query: The requirement IDs in this table are in the first column but the extraction put them in the requirement text. They should be separate.
This chunk has HTML entities that weren't decoded: & < '. Fix them.
scenarios.tests: HTML entity decoding failure, text normalization

scenarios.query: The extraction missed an entire page — page 23 content doesn't appear in any chunk. What happened?
scenarios.tests: page coverage gap, missing content detection

scenarios.query: This table has right-aligned numbers but the extraction left-aligned them and lost the decimal alignment. Show me the HTML.
The figure on page 12 wasn't extracted at all. Is it because the image was too small? What's the size threshold?
scenarios.tests: figure extraction coverage, size filter threshold

scenarios.query: The section titled 'References' contains the bibliography, but the section titled 'Appendix A' also has references mixed in. They should be separate.
Mathematical subscripts and superscripts were lost — 'H₂O' became 'H2O' and 'x²' became 'x2'. Where's the Unicode?
This table was extracted twice — once from S05 and once inline in the text from S07. Now there are duplicate chunks.
The extraction put figure captions in the wrong order — Figure 3's caption is attached to Figure 4's image.
Bullet points were collapsed into a single paragraph. The original had 8 distinct items, the extraction has one blob.
The watermark text 'DRAFT' appears in every chunk. It should have been stripped.
Links in the HTML content are broken — the href was stripped during extraction.
The table of contents was extracted as body text instead of being used to build the section hierarchy.
Code blocks in the document lost their formatting — indentation and line breaks are gone.
The extraction split a single sentence across two chunks. The first chunk ends mid-sentence.
scenarios.tests: sentence boundary detection at chunk splits

scenarios.query: Non-English characters (accented names, CJK text) were replaced with question marks or garbage.
The table has nested tables (a table within a cell). The extraction flattened it into nonsense.
Redacted/blacked-out content was OCR'd as random characters. Can we detect and skip redactions?
These two table chunks should be merged — they're the same table split across pages. Merge them.
Re-extract this document with the 'accurate' preset. The 'fast' preset missed too much.
Delete these 5 duplicate chunks and keep only the best version of each.
scenarios.tests: chunk deletion, dedup with quality selection

scenarios.query: The section hierarchy is flat — re-extract with font-size-based heading detection.
Run the normalize skill on all chunks from this document — there are encoding issues throughout.
This figure needs a better description. Re-run the VLM describer with a more specific prompt.
Re-extract all tables from this document using the 'lattice' strategy instead of 'stream'.
Split this oversized chunk into smaller pieces — it's 5000 words and recall can't use it effectively.
The embeddings for this document are all zero vectors. Re-generate them.
Add bridge tags to these chunks manually — the taxonomy extractor missed the cybersecurity domain.
This document was extracted from a scanned PDF. The OCR quality is low. Re-run with Tesseract instead of the default.
The page headers and footers are still in the text. Strip them and re-ingest.
Mark this document as superseded by a newer version. Keep it in the datalake but flag it.
The requirements extraction missed requirements in table format. Re-run S08 with table-aware mode.
Show me the 10 worst-quality documents by content coverage. Re-extract them all.
The section titles are all uppercase in the extraction but mixed case in the original. Fix the casing.
This equation was extracted as plain text 'E = mc^2' instead of LaTeX. Convert it.
Remove all chunks from this document — it was a draft that should never have been ingested.
scenarios.tests: document deletion, cascade to chunks and edges

scenarios.query: The figure on page 7 is a chart. Extract the data points from the chart into a table.
scenarios.tests: chart-to-table conversion, data extraction from figures

scenarios.query: Re-run the entire pipeline on this document and show me a before/after quality comparison.
Every time we extract a multi-column spec, the reading order is wrong. Create a lesson for this pattern.
scenarios.tests: failure pattern → lesson creation → memory store

scenarios.query: The pipeline keeps missing requirements in table footnotes. Learn from this so it doesn't happen again.
We've re-extracted this document 4 times. Are we converging or getting worse?
Collect all table extraction failures and train a classifier to predict which strategy to use.
The pipeline maps 'Para.' to 'Paragraph' but in P&W specs it means 'Requirement ID'. Fix the mapping and save as a lesson.
Build a gap analysis — what types of documents do we have the worst extraction quality for?
scenarios.tests: quality by document type, coverage gap analysis

scenarios.query: Compare our extraction accuracy against a manually annotated gold standard for this document.
The STIG checklists keep being classified as generic tables. Create a lesson to detect STIG format.
Show me all the lessons the pipeline has learned about table extraction. Are any contradictory?
scenarios.tests: lesson inventory, contradiction detection in lessons

scenarios.query: Generate a quality report across the entire datalake. Grade each document A through F.
The extraction improved for this document type after the last lesson. Show me the quality delta.
Which pipeline stage causes the most quality problems? Rank stages by failure frequency.
The VLM keeps hallucinating descriptions for technical diagrams. Collect the worst 10 and create a training set.
scenarios.tests: VLM failure collection → training data generation

scenarios.query: Cross-reference datalake requirements against SPARTA QRA controls. Flag contradictions.
Generate the certification-ready quality report. Content coverage must be >= 0.95 for all documents.
Find all chunks where recall returned irrelevant results for a known query. Create negative training examples.
How has extraction quality trended over the last month? Plot it.
Which lessons have been applied the most? Which haven't been triggered once?
The pipeline extracted a table perfectly in document A but badly in document B, even though the tables look identical. Why?
scenarios.tests: extraction inconsistency diagnosis, root cause analysis

scenarios.query: Build a confusion matrix for table extraction strategies (lattice vs stream vs hybrid). Which is best for which table type?
Find all content about corrosion resistance or environmental testing.
Show me all tables that have exactly 2 columns — they might be key-value pairs.
Find all chunks tagged with bridge tags. What's the tag distribution?
Which documents have no tables at all? Are they text-only reports?
scenarios.tests: table coverage gap, document type inference

scenarios.query: Find the shortest and longest chunks. What's the text length distribution?
Show me all chunks that contain URLs or hyperlinks in their text.
Find all content about quality assurance or quality control procedures.
How many chunks have taxonomy tags vs empty taxonomy? What percentage is enriched?
Find all documents that discuss supply chain or vendor management.
Show me chunks where the source_meta has page=0. That usually means the page wasn't detected.
Find a table with percentage values. Which items exceed 90%?
Show me a comparison table (Feature A vs Feature B columns). Summarize the differences.
Find a table with 'N/A' or '-' values. How many cells are missing data?
Show me a multi-row header table. Did the extraction correctly identify which rows are headers?
Find a table where row order matters (e.g., chronological, by priority). Is the order preserved?
Find all documents that discuss the same vulnerability. Compare their risk ratings.
Find all documents from the same source/organization. Are they consistent in formatting?
Which concepts appear in PDF documents but NOT in HTML documents? What's the format gap?
Find sections with the same title in different documents. Compare their content length and depth.
Build a topic map of the entire datalake. What are the 10 major themes?
Find all requirements that specify a tolerance (e.g., '+/- 0.5mm', 'within 2%').
Show me requirements that reference external standards by number (ISO, NIST, MIL-STD).
Find all 'performance' requirements vs 'design' requirements. How are they distributed?
Show me the requirements with the lowest confidence scores. Are they real requirements or false positives?
scenarios.tests: requirement confidence analysis, false positive detection

scenarios.query: Find requirements that are actually constraints (physical laws, regulatory mandates) vs design choices.
